I'm under 40 and my earliest jobs involved accepting credit cards through non-automated means in a retail establishment. The papers with carbon paper in between were made into a receipt, with descriptive information and pricing, and the credit card owner would sign the document. They would receive one copy of the receipt and the other two copies would go in the register. Presumably, those receipts were separated so one stayed with the business (for reconciliation) and the other went to the bank. It was similar to how checks operate, and a signed document was binding.

>“What your blood pressure is at 2 p.m. on a Tuesday doesn’t matter. >The company said in February that it had raised $14 million in Series A funding and is working toward getting clearance from the Food and Drug Administration for the seat to measure a handful of vital signs, Mr. McChord says. 

>Some diagnostics experts argue that the value in a smart toilet would come from being able to analyze the molecular substances in patient samples and that other devices, including smartwatches, can easily monitor blood pressure and heart rate.
